key_insight: Geometry-based fragmentation creates tunable, multiscale molecular representations without predefined chemical fragmentation rules for polymer property prediction.
engineering_relevance: Combining polymer sequence representations with 3D fragment information can improve prediction of several properties relevant to materials screening.
method: Formulate fragmentation as a radius-constrained optimization inspired by k-center, with fragment count determined by the radius.
Vary the radius to construct multiscale fragments using largely geometric information.
Integrate geometric fragment attention into a multimodal model combining p-SMILES and 3D conformations.
evidence_signal: Experiments on a benchmark polymer dataset report improved accuracy for several properties over p-SMILES-only models, with explainability analyses probing physical relevance.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify gains or establish how robust predictions are to conformer choice and fragmentation radius.
paper_title: Towards Multiscale Molecular Representation Learning through Geometry-Based Fragmentation for Polymer Property Prediction
